NEW DELHI: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh following violence in Pasighat during protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, officials said on Sunday.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) directed on Saturday that the two companies, comprising around 250 personnel, be airlifted from Navi Mumbai aboard an Indian Air Force transport aircraft. The units are expected to reach Pasighat and be deployed by Sunday, officials told news agency PTI.The RAF is a specialised anti-riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms.Several CRPF units are already deployed in the violence-hit areas. Arunachal Pradesh also has a permanent deployment of around two to three CRPF battalions.Officials said CRPF personnel had effectively handled the protests since Friday and prevented the violence from escalating. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes, they added.On Friday night, a mob torched an NHPC office and a police station and vandalised the residences of three political leaders, including the state BJP president, in East Siang district, according to Arunachal Pradesh Police officials.Arunachal chief minister Pema Khandu said the right to peaceful protest was an essential part of democracy, but stressed that demonstrations must remain within the bounds of the law and should not lead to property damage or disruption of public order.Describing the incidents in Pasighat as regrettable, Khandu appealed to all sections of society to maintain peace.According to a statement issued by the chief minister's Office (CMO), a 12-hour bandh in Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts over the proposed power project remained largely peaceful on Friday. However, violence broke out in Pasighat after the bandh ended and continued until 3.30 am on Saturday.Protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent in Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night, with "Gen Z" protesters allegedly setting fire to the NHPC office and a police station and vandalising and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president, police said.The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours into Saturday morning, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting", police said. A protester was hit in the leg by a tear gas shell and admitted to hospital.Following the violence, the East Siang district administration imposed restrictions on public gatherings and processions in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin, citing fears of vandalism, arson and a possible breach of law and order amid protests and bandh-related activities.India’s proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, planned across three districts of Arunachal, is being pitched as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam upstream. But the plan has faced resistance from indigenous tribes, who fear the reservoir could submerge villages and sever their deep-rooted ties with the river.Known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang enters Arunachal Pradesh near Gelling and flows for 294km before meeting the Dibang and Lohit rivers at Sadiya in Assam to form the Brahmaputra.
Article Summary: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh. The RAF is a specialised anti- riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday marked 12 years of his monthly radio programme, describing it as a “pilgrimage” that has allowed him to understand the efforts of people across the country and recognise their contributions.Addressing the 139th episode of the programme, PM Modi recalled thatbegan on the occasion of Vijayadashami 12 years ago and has continued uninterrupted since then. He thanked listeners for being fellow travellers and guides throughout the journey.“For me, ‘Mann Ki Baat’ has been a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the hard work, courage, commitment, dedication and spirit of service of the common man of our country,” the Prime Minister said.Drawing a parallel with India's longstanding tradition of pilgrimages, PM Modi said the programme had given him an opportunity to understand people's efforts closely and pay tribute to their contributions.“Our country has had a tradition of pilgrimages for centuries. For me, ‘Mann Ki Baat’ is not less than a pilgrimage, a journey to closely understand the efforts of people of the country and to pay tribute to their contributions,” he said.With Diwali and Chhath approaching, the Prime Minister urged people to maintain cleanliness in their surroundings and at places where they live.“The sacred festivals of Diwali and Chhath are just a few days away. Article Title: ‘Foreign-funded conspiracy to destabilise India’: Telangana BJP chief targets Congress over Jamia graffiti
Article Text:
Rao claimed that the opposition was encouraging students to act against national interests

Jamia protests trigger political row

NEW DELHI: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao on Sunday accused the Congress and the INDIA alliance of encouraging anti-national activities, alleging that the controversy over graffiti at Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia was part of a broader conspiracy to destabilise the country.Speaking to ANI, Rao claimed that radical networks within student groups were being supported by opposition political parties. He also alleged that the campus demonstrations were part of a foreign-sponsored effort to create unrest in India, though he did not provide evidence to substantiate the claim.“Writing on the walls of Jamia Millia University in Delhi, all these things are now being exposed because there are people who are part of the ‘Tukde-Tukde’ gang and anti-national gangs who are among the students, and they are in support of Sharjeel Imam, who has actually been involved in several anti-national activities,” Rao said.Targeting the Congress and other INDIA alliance parties over their alleged silence on the controversy, Rao claimed that the opposition was encouraging students to act against national interests.“This slogan shows that the Congress and the INDIA alliance, which are silent on this issue, show how they are inciting students and everyone in the country to go against the interests of the nation and indulge in anti-national activities,” he said.Rao further alleged that the protests were designed to create anarchy and were being sponsored by a foreign country to destabilise India.The BJP leader’s remarks come amid heightened tensions at Jamia Millia Islamia, where university authorities recently shifted classes to an online format, citing student safety amid ongoing campus demonstrations.The controversy has also drawn Congress leaders into the dispute. Congress MP Imran Masood, who visited the university to meet protesting students on Friday, denied that slogans calling for a “free Kashmir” had been raised during the demonstrations. Delhi Police detained Masood during his visit.“No slogans calling for a ‘free Kashmir’ were raised there, not a single one. I stood up in front of everyone and strongly condemned such slogans, stating that Kashmir is an integral part of India,” Masood told ANI.Since Oct 12, students have been on a sit-in and hunger strike, which has grown into Jamia's biggest student protest since the anti-CAA agitation. Jamia has not had an elected union since 2006, when it was dissolved following violence. It is one of Delhi's few central universities without an elected union.
Article Summary: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao accused the Congress and the INDIA alliance of encouraging anti-national activities. Rao claimed that radical networks within student groups were being supported by opposition political parties. He also alleged that the campus demonstrations were part of a foreign- sponsored effort to create unrest in India.

Article Title: ‘Saddam Hussein opened a cheesecake factory’: Obama’s jibe at Trump’s White House
Article Text:
‘Jawlines and testosterone’: Obama takes a dig at Hegseth amid Iran conflict

Obama targets Pete Hegseth

What are US midterm elections

Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House, saying Trump has "got the White House looking like former Iraq President Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory".Obama made the remarks while campaigning for the midterm elections in Ohio. He mocked Trump’s changes to the White House, saying the president appeared more interested in renovations than other matters."I don't know if you've noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. He should be on HGTV. The guy’s building a ballroom that’s bigger than the White House. Paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there’s gold everywhere! What’s up with the gold? Everything—more gold!” Obama said.He continued his criticism, drawing laughter and applause from the crowd. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere."After his speech, Obama took to social media platform X to urge voters to support Democratic candidates in Ohio’s gubernatorial and Senate elections."Ohio, let's do what we can to elect Amy Acton as your next Governor and Sherrod Brown as your next US Senator! They’ve dedicated their lives to fighting on behalf of all Ohioans," Obama wrote.Obama also stressed the importance of grassroots campaigning and high voter turnout, saying collective action could help bring about positive change in the country."If we’re willing to organise and mobilise, if we’re willing to turn out in big numbers in Ohio and across this country, if we’re willing to vote for change and vote for Democrats up and down the ballot, then this election might just mark the moment this country began moving in a better direction," he stated.He ended his message by urging voters to make sure they cast their ballots.Obama also criticised US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, linking the ongoing conflict with Iran to concerns over the country's military preparedness."Hundreds of Americans have been wounded. We have run down our stock of missiles, and Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, you’ve got the defense secretary who’s squarely focused on important matters like the jawlines and testosterone levels of our troops," he said.US midterm elections take place every four years, halfway through a president’s four-year term. They are seen as an important test of public opinion on the president and the ruling party.The elections determine control of Congress, with all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and roughly one-third of the Senate seats up for election. The results can influence the president’s ability to pass laws and implement policies.
Article Summary: Former US President Barack Obama took a dig at Donald Trump over his renovation plans for the White House. Obama made the remarks while campaigning for the midterm elections in Ohio. He also criticised US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, linking the ongoing conflict with Iran to concerns over the country's military preparedness.

Article Title: Violent protests in Arunachal against Siang dam; MLAs’ homes looted, NHPC set ablaze
Article Text:
The mob also hurled stones at a hospital where injured central force personnel had been taken. At least nine police vehicles were damaged

CM expresses concern, offers to meet groups for talks





GUWAHATI/ITANAGAR: Protests against Arunachal Pradesh's proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent at Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night, with "Gen Z" protesters allegedly torching the NHPC office and a police station, and vandalising and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president, police said.The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours early Saturday, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting", police said. A protester was hit in the leg by a tear gas shell and admitted to hospital. The East Siang district administration imposed restrictions on public gatherings and processions in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin, citing apprehensions of vandalism, arson and a potential breach of law and order following protests and bandh-related activities.In an executive order issued Saturday, deputy commissioner Jayanti Pertin said the restrictions would come into effect from 5pm on Oct 24 and remain in force until withdrawn or modified.The violence began after a 12-hour bandh called by Adi Baane Kebang United, along with other organisations, against the proposed project ended peacefully at 5pm. The bandh, however, was not observed in Pasighat area.One of our deputy SPs suffered a head injury and has been evacuated to Dibrugarh, where he is being treated.Central police force personnel were also badly hurt, Pasighat IGP (central range) Hibu Tamang said.The mob also pelted stones at a hospital where injured central force personnel had been taken. At least nine police vehicles were damaged. The groups dispersed around 4am.“A youth group calling itself ‘Gen Z’ suddenly emerged and sat on a dharna on the Mebo side. Around 2pm, this group entered Pasighat jurisdiction. They blocked the Pasighat-Boleng highway and did not let traffic pass. They had no clear demand. They said they would sit on a dharna indefinitely, and there was also slogan-shouting,” Tamang said.He said police and civil authorities persuaded the group to leave the highway for two hours without any result. “As darkness fell, the group became very violent and unruly. A violent mob of 200-300 began pelting stones at police and the magistrate. Some of them were carrying liquor and beer bottles in their hands and were intoxicated. Police handled it gently and did nothing other than using tear gas,” the IGP said.Police said that they documented the incident on video and photographs.Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu expressed concern and offered to meet the groups for talks.
Article Summary: Protests against Arunachal Pradesh's proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project turned violent at Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night. "Gen Z" protesters allegedly torched the NHPC office and a police station, and vandalised and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president. The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours early Saturday, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting"

Article Title: 'Told to post it': Delhi youth arrested in ex-CM Siddaramaiah sting clip case; Bengaluru court grants 22-year-old conditional bail
Article Text:
Accused Ritesh Pandey was granted conditional bail.

'Told to post clips'





BENGALURU: Sleuths from the Central Crime Branch (CCB), Bengaluru, picked up a 22-year-old man in Delhi late Friday night in connection with the alleged sting operation involving former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah , marking the first arrest in the case. He was brought to Bengaluru early Saturday morning and produced in court.A local court granted accused Ritesh Pandey conditional bail, directing him to inform the police before leaving Bengaluru and appear for questioning whenever summoned.Police sources said Pandey uploaded the contentious video on multiple social media platforms, including a YouTube channel named ‘Karnataka Honeytrap’.He allegedly told investigators that Prajwal Prasad, a member of a political party’s social media wing, had instructed him to upload the clip.According to an investigating officer, Pandey bought a used Android phone for Rs 15,000 from a shop in Delhi’s Karol Bagh market and used a USB device to upload the video. Police have recovered CCTV footage showing him buying the phone and seized a copy of the purchase bill, the officer added.Police have also issued notices to two members of a political party’s social media team, Mohan Gowda and Chandan, seeking information about who supplied the video to Pandey. Both have been unresponsive, police sources said.A senior IPS officer said investigators had questioned those connected with the case, including people who appeared or were heard in the video.
Article Summary: Sleuths from the Central Crime Branch (CCB), Bengaluru, picked up a 22-year-old man in Delhi late Friday night in connection with the alleged sting operation involving former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah. He was brought to Bengaluru early Saturday morning and produced in court. Accused Ritesh Pandey was granted conditional bail.

Article Title: How Bengaluru advocate’s death turned into a murder probe: 'Fight over auto fare, suspected heart attack, then a post-mortem twist'
Article Text:
Police have taken Pruthviraj Appajigowda into custody.

Found unconscious on Outer Ring Road

Argument over fare allegedly led to assault

Missing phone, cash allegations under probe





BENAGLURU: An argument over an auto-rickshaw fare, a suspected heart attack and a post-mortem twist have turned the case of a 43-year-old Bengaluru advocate into a murder probe.Police have taken Pruthviraj Appajigowda, 31, an auto-rickshaw driver from Gollarahatti on Magadi Road, into custody in connection with the death of Sri Ram, a resident of Kengunte.Investigators are also looking for other auto drivers who were allegedly present during the confrontation.Sri Ram was found unconscious on Nagarabavi Outer Ring Road on the morning of October 9. Hoysala police personnel on patrol rushed him to a nearby private hospital, where he died later that day.Initially, his death was suspected to be due to a heart attack. However, his family noticed injury marks on his body and approached Annapoorneshwarinagar police, suspecting foul play.The body was sent for a post-mortem examination. The report, which arrived recently, indicated that the advocate had died due to a blood clot in the brain, prompting investigators to look into the circumstances surrounding his death.The investigation led police to Pruthviraj, who allegedly attacked Sri Ram near Ambedkar Institute of Technology in Mallathahalli.According to an investigating officer, Sri Ram had asked Pruthviraj for a ride but disagreed with the fare quoted by the driver. He then walked away, saying he would take another auto-rickshaw. Pruthviraj allegedly followed him and attacked him, pushing him to the ground and causing internal head injuries.“There was a heated argument between the two over the tariff. Sri Ram had asked Pruthviraj for a ride and did not agree to the price quoted by him. Saying he will catch another auto, Sri Ram walked away. Angered over the refusal, Pruthviraj followed him and attacked. Sri Ram sustained internal head injuries when Pruthviraj pushed him to the ground. There were few more auto drivers with Pruthviraj when the incident took place and we are looking for them,” an investigating officer said.Police subsequently traced the auto-rickshaw and its driver, leading to Pruthviraj being taken into custody.Investigators are also examining allegations that Sri Ram’s mobile phone and some cash went missing after the incident.“There are allegations that accused person had taken away Sri Ram’s mobile phone and some cash. We are looking into it,” the officer added.Police are searching for the other auto-rickshaw drivers allegedly present during the confrontation as they investigate the circumstances leading to the advocate’s death.
Article Summary: Police have taken Pruthviraj Appajigowda, 31, into custody in connection with the death of Sri Ram, a resident of Kengunte. Sri Ram was found unconscious on Nagarabavi Outer Ring Road on the morning of October 9. Police are searching for other auto drivers allegedly present during the confrontation.

Article Title: Farooq Abdullah's comments on Pakistan and Kashmir draw flak
Article Text:
Farooq also mentioned the Chittisinghpura massacre in which 36 Sikhs were killed in south Kashmir.

SRINAGAR: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday declared that Pakistan had “saved” Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at international forums, while being careful to say that “otherwise their (Pakistan’s) intentions are not good”.His statement drew flak from BJP, which slammed it as “seditious and anti-national”.“If you do not remain (committed to NC), you will be erased. Even our identity will disappear. Nothing will be left. They are silent today because there is noise in the world and our neighbour is constantly behind it. Everywhere they say ‘the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made’. That is what is saving us…,” Farooq told a meeting of NC workers in Baramulla. The words “they” and “their” were seen as an allusion to the Centre.Farooq’s son, J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah, had not reacted to his father’s remarks till late Saturday.Farooq urged NC workers and legislators to remain loyal to the party, whether in power or not, as he touched on a range of issues in his speech. “Hold on to the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you remain truthful and stand up for what is right, your future will never be secure,” the veteran said.Citing the 1947 tribal invasion, Farooq condemned the “atrocities” inflicted on Kashmiris by the raiders from Pakistan”. He paid tributes to Maqbool Sherwani, an NC worker who died staving off the intruders, saying his “sacrifice helped stop the raiders in Baramulla and save Kashmir”.Farooq also mentioned the Chittisinghpura massacre in which 36 Sikhs were killed in south Kashmir on March 20, 2000, during then US President Bill Clinton’s visit to India. He said a subsequent judicial inquiry had found that five men accused of carrying out the killings were not the perpetrators but shopkeepers “who had been picked up by police and killed”. According to Farooq, the inquiry judge should have investigated the massacre itself but was “told from Delhi” not to.BJP decried Farooq’s comments. Party functionary Ravinder Raina called them “treason” and asked how Pakistan could ever be a well-wisher of the people of J&K. “Farooq Abdullah chose Baramulla for his pro-Pakistan remarks just two days after the anniversary of Pakistan’s Oct 22, 1947 invasion of J&K. This is the land of Maqbool Sherwani, who stood against invaders, not a stage to whitewash Pakistan’s bloody history,” J&K BJP spokesman Sajid Yousuf Shah said.Peoples Conference’s Imran Reza Ansari cautioned against following Farooq. “If a common Kashmiri speaks in a similar tone, govt will in seconds put that person in detention under PSA or UAPA. Please save your children and your families. Don’t emulate this person,” Ansari said.
Article Summary: Farooq Abdullah said Pakistan had “saved” Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at international forums. His statement drew flak from BJP, which slammed it as ‘seditious and anti-national’ “If you do not remain (committed to NC), you will be erased. Even our identity will disappear. Nothing will be left,” he said.

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Saturday strongly criticised National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah's remark claiming Pakistan was “protecting” the people of Jammu and Kashmir by repeatedly raising the " Kashmir issue " at international forums. BJP leaders accused Abdullah of echoing Pakistan's narrative.BJP Jammu and Kashmir leader Ravinder Raina called his remarks an “act of treason” and questioned how Pakistan could be considered a well-wisher of Kashmiris. Raina termed Abdullah's statement “highly condemnable and unfortunate”, alleging that Pakistan had supported terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir for decades.“The statement made by Dr Farooq Abdullah regarding Kashmir and Pakistan is highly condemnable and unfortunate. In fact, Dr Farooq Abdullah has committed an act of treason," Raina said."Pakistan is the killer of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Over the last 35 years, Pakistan has sought to turn Jammu and Kashmir into a graveyard and a cremation ground. This is the very same Pakistan that has fostered terrorism within Jammu and Kashmir—providing training, bombs, guns, pistols, ammunition, and grenades to terrorists. How could Pakistan ever be a well-wisher to the people of Jammu and Kashmir?" he added.Uttar Pradesh minister Suresh Kumar Khanna also accused Abdullah of exploiting Kashmiris throughout his political career. He said the region's integration into the national mainstream under the Modi government was in the best interests of its people.“It is people like Farooq Abdullah who have exploited Kashmir throughout their lives. Farooq Abdullah is responsible for reducing Kashmiris to second-class citizens, and he ought not to be making such statements. It is precisely because of India’s diversity that Kashmir is now integrated into the nation’s mainstream, and every citizen of Kashmir enjoys the same rights as those in the rest of India. Therefore, the current situation in Kashmir—brought about by the Modi government—is what is truly in the best interest of the Kashmiri people. Today, the people of Kashmir are at their happiest, thanks to the Modi government,” Khanna said.BJP leader Altaf Thakur also condemned Abdullah's remarks, calling them an attack on India's unity and integrity. He demanded action against the National Conference chief.“This is an open rebellion against the country. His statement is against the unity and integrity of the country. The National Conference has always been anti-country. The statement made by Farooq Abdullah is completely an anti-country statement. Action should be taken against him,” Thakur said.Chhattisgarh deputy chief minister Vijay Sharma questioned Abdullah's allegations about the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir, asking whether he considered himself separate from India.“If we point out that they lack love for the country, they immediately start complaining that such things are being said about them. He himself served as chief minister, and now his son is chief minister. He has full access to all resources—from across India and everywhere else. Yet, he still makes such accusations. If he claims that India’s intentions were not good, does that mean he views himself as separate from India? He should learn from his own son, Omar Abdullah,” Sharma said.Janata Dal (United) state president G M Shaheen also criticised Abdullah, questioning why he continued to echo Pakistan's narrative despite having held several constitutional positions.“When a leader like Farooq Abdullah makes such a statement and supports Pakistan, what else can I call it but a misfortune? He has served as a chief minister, a member of the Rajya Sabha, and a member of parliament; he has worked within the framework of the country’s Constitution, yet, he chooses to speak the language of Pakistan. It is truly shameful. If Jammu and Kashmir is safe, it is because of India. Why does he always echo Pakistan’s narrative? The militancy that has plagued Kashmir since the 1990s was, in part, a consequence of his government. Whenever these people have come to power, they have invariably begun to speak the language of Pakistan. This is nothing new for Farooq Abdullah, but the nation should hold him accountable,” Shaheen said.Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) leader Vinod Bansal also condemned Abdullah's comments, asserting that Jammu and Kashmir would always remain an integral part of India. He questioned the suggestion that Pakistan was protecting Kashmiris.“Kashmir was, is, and will always remain an integral part of India. They live in India and sing praises of Pakistan. Is Kashmir safe because of Pakistan, or is Kashmir safe by showing India's strength to Pakistan? If this is his statement, then there is no greater treason than this,” Bansal said.Congress leaders also disagreed with Abdullah's remarks about Pakistan but raised concerns about the political and administrative situation in Jammu and Kashmir, particularly the delay in restoring statehood.Congress leader Ravinder Sharma said Jammu and Kashmir was an integral part of India and accused Pakistan of promoting terrorism. Citing the Shimla Agreement, he argued that Pakistan had no right to raise the Kashmir issue. He also highlighted concerns about the treatment of minorities and the continued denial of statehood to the region.“Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India, and it will remain an integral part. Pakistan spreads terrorism. Pakistan has no right or claim to raise the issue of Jammu and Kashmir, especially following the Shimla Agreement, in which it was agreed in writing that bilateral issues would be addressed through direct, bilateral engagement. Thirdly, regarding Farooq Abdullah’s remarks: he pointed to the disenfranchisement of minority voters, the use of bulldozers against minorities, and other forms of oppression, noting that there is an elected government in Kashmir. The Congress party is also fighting for this, demanding to know why, despite repeated promises, an undertaking given to the Supreme Court, and discussions in Parliament, statehood is still being denied to the people of Jammu and Kashmir. In that context, we also recognise that the people of Jammu and Kashmir are facing oppression,” Sharma said.Congress leader Rashid Alvi also disagreed with Abdullah's position, pointing to the situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) while criticising the BJP government's handling of Jammu and Kashmir.“I do not agree with Farooq Abdullah on this. There is no doubt that the BJP government has committed excesses in Kashmir. But what is happening in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)? People there regularly protest against the Pakistani government. If the people in PoK are unhappy and dissatisfied with the Pakistani government, what can Pakistan do about our Kashmir?” Alvi said.Abdullah said Pakistan's repeated efforts to raise the Kashmir issue internationally were putting pressure on India. He alleged that the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir were not good and urged people to stand up for their rights.“What can you expect from Delhi? You must have the courage to stand up to them and fight. If you do not, you will be wiped out. Your name and identity will disappear, and no one will even remember you. Our neighbour is constantly after them. It goes everywhere, saying that the Kashmir issue has not been resolved. It is protecting us; otherwise, their intentions are not good. They say one thing but do something entirely different,” Abdullah said.He also called on people to stand by the truth, warning that their future would remain insecure unless they spoke out.“You must have the courage to stand by the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you speak the truth and stand firm by it, your future will never be secure,” he said.Apart from his comments on Pakistan and the Centre, Abdullah raised concerns about the mandatory two-year service requirement for doctors who pursue MBBS, MD or MS courses in Jammu and Kashmir. He alleged that a file related to the policy had been pending with the Lieutenant Governor for a year.“Doctors who come from outside Jammu and Kashmir to pursue MBBS, MD, or MS courses, as well as students who study medicine here, are required to serve for two years in villages, hospitals, and other areas across the region. If they fail to fulfil this requirement, they must pay Rs 50 Lakh to the administration. This is a region where a file has been pending with the Lieutenant Governor for a year, yet it has still not been approved. This is the state of affairs here. What can you expect from Delhi? Can you really expect them to deliver justice to you?” Abdullah said.
Article Summary: BJP leaders accused Abdullah of echoing Pakistan's narrative. BJP Jammu and Kashmir leader Ravinder Raina called his remarks an “act of treason” Uttar Pradesh minister Suresh Kumar Khanna accused him of exploiting Kashmiris throughout his political career.

Article Title: ‘Prioritise welfare over military directives’: India raps Pak on minority rights at UN
Article Text:

India slams Pakistan over minority rights

India asserts climate justice and judicial independence

NEW DELHI: India tore into Pakistan at the United Nations for exploiting the international forum to spread propaganda while failing to protect its own citizens. New Delhi reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir remains an integral and inalienable part of India and demanded that Pakistan vacate all territories under its illegal occupation.Speaking at an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct and said its representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military."Pakistan predictably misused the forum for propaganda. Jammu & Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India. Pakistan must vacate the territory under its illegal occupation," Puri said.He further said Pakistani representatives would do well to look inwards and address the concerns of their own citizens rather than act on military directives.Puri underlined that protecting minority rights was primarily the sovereign responsibility of individual states, guided by the principle of sovereign equality.He said India's civilisational tradition of diversity was reflected in its constitutional safeguards for religious and linguistic minorities.He also highlighted the substantial contributions made by minorities to India's national development, including at the highest levels of government and key institutions.The latest confrontation followed India's strong rebuke to Pakistan at the UN on October 23 over its treatment of religious minorities. New Delhi accused Islamabad of failing to protect vulnerable communities while attempting to lecture India on religious freedom, burial rights and minority protections.During an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief, India's First Secretary at the UN mission, Bhavika Mangalanandan, challenged the report's approach to religious discrimination during the Covid-19 pandemic and its advocacy concerning funeral rights for terrorists.Mangalanandan argued that the report appeared to place disproportionate emphasis on discriminatory practices and shortcomings in countries in the Global South while overlooking similar tragedies in developed nations.Separately, India also defended its approach to climate change at the UN General Assembly, stressing the importance of equity, climate justice and sustainable development.Deputy secretary Barkha Tamrakar delivered India's statement before the Third Committee on the report of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers, titled “An urgent and existential threat: the role of justice systems in addressing the climate crisis.”Tamrakar described climate change as a serious global challenge with consequences for development, livelihoods and human rights. She said India's response was guided by equity, climate justice, sustainable development and the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC).She highlighted the Constitution, environmental legislation, the National Green Tribunal and an independent judiciary as key safeguards supporting environmental protection in India.Tamrakar also noted that the Supreme Court had recognised the fundamental rights to life and equality as essential protections against the adverse effects of climate change.On judicial independence, she pointed to transparent, institutionally supervised training programmes, including those conducted by the National Judicial Academy, as measures to strengthen impartiality and safeguard the independence of the judiciary.
Article Summary: New Delhi reiterates that Jammu and Kashmir remains an integral and inalienable part of India. India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct. Puri said Pakistani representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military.

Article Title: RG Kar victim's parents question ex-principal Sandip Ghosh's bail; citizens' groups plan CBI office march

The parents of the RG Kar rape-and-murder victim on Saturday questioned the bail granted to former hospital principal Sandip Ghosh in a corruption case, while announcing renewed calls for accountability in the investigation into their daughter's death.Meanwhile, two citizens' groups, 'Voice of Abhaya' and 'Voice of Women', have announced a protest march to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) office on November 12, starting from RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The organisers have appealed to citizens, particularly women, to join the demonstration and press for action in the case."We appeal to citizens from all sections of society, especially women, to come out on the streets on November 12 and show that they do not have to depend on any government to get their demands fulfilled. Let the CBI know that despite attempts to destroy, withhold or suppress evidence, people are still protesting and are on the streets. There is no room for despair," one of the organisers said, as quoted by PTI.The groups urged people not to lose hope and called on the investigating agency to act on the evidence.The proposed demonstration comes amid mounting criticism from the victim's family and sections of the medical community over the pace of the investigation.The Joint Platform of Doctors had also criticised the CBI last week following the Supreme Court's decision to grant bail to Ghosh, warning of a larger agitation over the slow progress of the probe.The victim's mother, Ratna Debnath, who is now a BJP MLA, expressed anger over Ghosh's bail and questioned why those who were with her daughter in the hours before her death had not been arrested."If everyone had been arrested at the time instead of allowing evidence to be destroyed, the situation might have been different. In every case, the last-seen theory is examined. Those present with my daughter must be questioned. The doctors have said that she died between midnight and 6 am. Who was with her during that period? Why have they not been arrested? Is it because they are doctors? My daughter was also a doctor," she said.Debnath also demanded action against those she alleged had ordered the destruction of evidence following the crime."Who were the people who directed that everything be destroyed so quickly? The then health minister, the health secretary NS Nigam and Sandip Ghosh... those responsible must be identified. The main conspirators must be brought to justice," she said.The victim's father also criticised the investigation and said Ghosh should have been sentenced to life imprisonment in the case, while expressing faith that justice would eventually be delivered."He should have been sentenced to life imprisonment in this case," he said.Last week, the father had questioned the CBI's handling of the investigation and demanded that Ghosh be chargesheeted in the rape-and-murder case. He also said the agency's investigating officer, Monish Upadhyay, had told him that there was little the CBI could do at present and that the process would take time.The father had expressed concern over the agency's accountability, saying, "If 1.47 billion people place their trust in an agency, how can they continue to have faith in it if such negligence persists? The government is not responsible; the investigating agency is."Debnath had similarly said at the time that the government could not be held directly responsible for the CBI's actions, describing it as an independent investigating agency that would have to answer for its work.The victim's father also questioned the continued tenure of West Bengal health secretary NS Nigam. "He will not remain in the post. The chief minister has said that if evidence is found, he can be removed," he said.BJP leader Rahul Sinha also expressed surprise over Ghosh's bail but said the decision rested with the judiciary."We were also surprised that Sandip Ghosh got bail. I would clearly say that it would have been better if he had not been granted bail. But can any of us interfere with a judge? The decision to grant or deny bail rests entirely with the judiciary, and obtaining bail is also an individual's legal right. I can say clearly that nobody in Bengal is happy with this bail order," Sinha told reporters.The Supreme Court granted bail to Ghosh on October 17 in the case concerning alleged financial irregularities at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital and the manipulation of merit scores to accommodate undeserving candidates.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale allowed his plea challenging the Calcutta High Court's February 23 order denying bail. The apex court took note of the period Ghosh had spent in custody and the pace of the trial, observing that he had been incarcerated for more than two years while only seven of the 147 witnesses had been examined.Ghosh had resigned as the hospital's principal after the rape and murder of the postgraduate trainee doctor in August 2024. He was subsequently arrested in connection with alleged financial irregularities at the institution. The CBI had also arrested Ghosh and Abhijit Mondal, the then officer-in-charge of Tala police station, over allegations linked to evidence tampering and lapses in the investigation.Junior doctor Aniket Mahata, a prominent figure in the RG Kar movement, had also criticised the bail decision last week, saying it had renewed anger among doctors and calling for a united fight for justice.
Article Summary: Parents of RG Kar rape-and-murder victim question bail of former hospital principal Sandip Ghosh. Two citizens' groups announce protest march to CBI office on November 12. Demonstration comes amid mounting criticism from victim's family and medical community over pace of investigation.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Saturday questioned the decision to allow US national Matthew VanDyke, an accused in the Myanmar arms training case, to return to his home country, asking why a foreign national accused of terrorism was being granted such liberty while young activists protesting against alleged “vote chori” were being detained.Congress general secretary in charge of communications Jairam Ramesh raised the issue in a post on X, referring to VanDyke's release and the extension of permission for him and six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India until February 24 next year.“US national Matthew VanDyke, arrested for conspiring to carry out terrorist activities against India, was released yesterday and allowed to return home for 4 months. Why has such liberty been extended to a foreign national accused of terrorism?” Ramesh asked.He also criticised the government's handling of protests against alleged electoral irregularities.“This even as the government has shown no hesitation in detaining and arresting youth activists and peaceful protesters during the anti-vote chori protests this past month,” he said.Ramesh further pointed to the issue being raised during US secretary of state Marco Rubio 's visit to India in May, noting that the American official had visited again this week.Ramesh had previously accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being a “compromised PM” following VanDyke's release in September.The Congress leader had claimed that Rubio raised the matter during his May visit to India and that US ambassador to India Sergio Gor also took it up with foreign secretary Vikram Misri.On September 8, Ramesh claimed that charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) had been dropped against VanDyke. He alleged that this contrasted with what he described as the widespread misuse of the law against Indian citizens and delays in such cases.After VanDyke was released on September 24, Ramesh alleged that the prime minister had “failed” to protect India's elections, institutions and national security.A Delhi court on Friday extended until February 24, 2027, the permission granted to VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) continues its probe into the Myanmar arms training case.Special Judge Prashant Sharma passed the order after hearing applications filed by the seven accused. The proceedings were held in-camera.The NIA sought additional time to investigate several aspects of the case, with its counsel Rahul Tyagi making submissions to that effect. The agency told the court that further investigation was needed to verify alleged offences under the UAPA in connection with the import and recovery of large quantities of drones and accessories through India.VanDyke appeared in person before the court on Friday and was permitted to return to the US.The other six accused attended the hearing through video conferencing, citing health issues.The seven foreign nationals had earlier been permitted to stay in their home countries until October 23 after seeking six weeks to meet their families.The NIA has alleged that VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals entered India on tourist visas, travelled to the northeastern region without the required permits and crossed from Mizoram into Myanmar, where they allegedly trained ethnic armed organisations.The accused were arrested on March 13 over allegations of training insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.The agency had initially invoked provisions of the UAPA, including those relating to conspiracy.However, its chargesheet did not include the UAPA provisions and instead invoked Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act. These provisions cover offences that can be compounded before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO).The NIA had previously indicated that its investigation into the alleged terror-related aspects was continuing and that further allegations could be included in a supplementary chargesheet.
Article Summary: Congress asks why US national accused in Myanmar arms case was allowed to return home. Court allows seven accused to remain abroad till February 24. Jairam Ramesh also criticised the government's handling of protests against alleged electoral irregularities. He had previously accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being a ‘compromised PM’

India on Saturday condemned a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan that killed eight people and injured several others, expressing solidarity with the Jordanian government and people.In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "India unequivocally condemns the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan on 23rd October 2026, which resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured in this cowardly attack. India stands firmly with the Government and the friendly people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in this difficult hour. We also reaffirm our strong commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations."External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also condemned the attack and expressed condolences to the victims' families.The attack took place on Friday at a church in the village of Hammoud in the Karak governorate, where gunmen opened fire on a funeral procession. The death toll rose to eight on Saturday after one of the injured victims, who was in critical condition, died, Health Minister Ibrahim al-Bdour told AFP.Another 26 people remain hospitalised, including one in critical condition, the minister said.Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya described the shooting as a terrorist attack and said security forces were working to track down those responsible."A terrorist group has carried out a horrific act, one that is condemned in every respect, and the security services are working round the clock to track them down," he told a press conference.King Abdullah II, who visited the wounded at a hospital in Karak, also condemned the attack and said on X that the shooting "will be met with the harshest retaliation".Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered three days of national mourning beginning Friday, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public institutions.Karak is home to a significant Christian community in Jordan, a Muslim-majority country where Christians account for between two and three per cent of the population.

The Himveers of ITBP have played a vital role in safeguarding India’s borders in the harshest climatic conditions. They have also made significant contributions to internal security operations, including efforts to combat Left Wing Extremism,” Singh said.He added that their courage, professionalism and commitment to duty reflected the finest traditions of service to the nation.Kiren Rijiju also greeted the Himveers, invoking the force's motto, “शौर्य-दृढ़ता-कर्मनिष्ठा” (valour, steadfastness and devotion to duty).“On the occasion of ITBP Raising Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to the Himveers of @ITBP_official. The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Friday that the situation along the India-China border gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns.“Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC),” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.Jaiswal also said the two countries had agreed to discuss ways to improve their understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas to strengthen border management. He stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral relations.ITBP director general Shatrujeet Kapur had recently spoken about continuing confrontations with Chinese troops at several locations along the border in Arunachal Pradesh.He also said the force had raised drone platoons in all its border units and developed a new 'Strike' course to better handle battles similar to the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.

NEW DELHI: Kerala governor Om Prakash Mathur's reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only has sparked a political controversy, with Congress leader K C Venugopal accusing him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda.Mathur, the former Sikkim governor, directed that non-vegetarian food should not be prepared or served in the Lok Bhavan kitchen. The reports surfaced on Thursday, a day before he assumed office, news agency PTI reported.Reacting to the reports shortly after Mathur was sworn in as the 29th governor of Keralam, AICC general secretary Venugopal alleged that the decision went beyond the governor's personal food preferences and infringed on individual freedom.Keralam has a diverse food culture and abundant fish resources as a coastal state, Venugopal said, adding that people had the freedom to choose between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food."Any attempt to restrict the food habits Keralites are accustomed to or dictate what they should eat from now on cannot be accepted," he said as quoted by PTI.Venugopal argued that restrictions that "intrude" into people's food choices and seek to erase Keralam's traditional way of life violate fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.He alleged that the governor was using his authority to "curtail" individual freedom instead of protecting people's right to decide what to eat and how to live."This is a continuation of the unconstitutional interests of the Sangh Parivar. This is the first step towards implementing the saffron agenda of the Sangh Parivar in Keralam," the Alappuzha MP alleged.While acknowledging Mathur's right to follow a vegetarian diet, Venugopal said the governor should not impose his personal preferences on the Lok Bhavan kitchen, whose employees include Keralites. He urged Mathur to withdraw any decision restricting food choices.Sources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian and had directed that non-vegetarian food not be prepared in the kitchen where his meals were cooked.They clarified that the kitchen's food was served only to the governor and a few members of his personal staff. Other employees either brought food from home or ate outside, and no restrictions had been imposed on their food choices, the sources said as cited by PTI.They added that fish and meat dishes had been prepared in the Lok Bhavan kitchen during the tenure of some previous governors.
Article Summary: Kerala Governor Om Prakash Mathur’s reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only sparks a row. Congress leader K C Venugopal accuses him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda. Sources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. Article Title: "Exchanged s*x for platforming any person": Kai Cenat takes legal action against former friend Reggie over alleged false claims on social media
Article Text:
Kai Cenat’s cease-and-desist letter targets Reggie’s allegations

Reggie responds to Kai Cenat’s legal move with a music video

Kai Cenat’s fallout with former friend Reggie has moved beyond social media arguments, with a reported cease-and-desist letter raising the stakes in their public dispute. The legal move comes after weeks of controversy over serious allegations involving the popular streamer. Kai’s legal team has denied the claims and demanded that Reggie remove related posts and videos. Reggie, however, appears ready to fight back, publicly discussing the legal notice and releasing a music video that seems to draw inspiration from their ongoing conflict.According to TMZ, Kai Cenat’s legal team sent Reggie a cease-and-desist letter dated October 2, accusing him of making false and misleading statements online. The letter reportedly demands that Reggie stop repeating the disputed claims and remove social media content connected to them.Kai’s representatives strongly rejected allegations that he engaged in pedophilia or exchanged sexual favors for opportunities on his platform.“We want to be unequivocal: the suggestion that Mr. Cenat has ever engaged in any form of pedophilia, or exchanged s*x for platforming any person, is categorically false,” the statement read.The letter reportedly argues that Reggie has not supplied evidence to support his claims. Kai’s attorney also described the allegations as “nonsense” and said they had harmed the streamer’s reputation and business relationships.The document reportedly raises additional concerns about alleged threats against Kai and people associated with him. According to the letter, the situation has created safety concerns for employees and disrupted business operations.However, a cease-and-desist letter is a legal demand, not a court ruling. The allegations and denials remain distinct from any finding of legal responsibility.Reggie has shown little sign of stepping away from the dispute publicly. Before news of the reported legal action emerged, he shared what he described as court documents on Instagram and suggested he was prepared to involve his lawyers.“Finally finna call my lawyers rn!!”He later addressed the cease-and-desist in an Instagram Story, writing, “Kai Ceant sent a cease and desist but he never addressed the pdf stuff lol ok ‘watch me.’”Reggie has also released a YouTube music video for his track ‘Watch Me!’ Its visuals appear to reference the moment he was served with legal papers near the AMP House. The video also mentions Kai’s clothing brand, VIVET, and fellow streamer RaKai, bringing the dispute into his music.The developments have sparked divided reactions online. Some social media users have praised Kai’s decision to seek legal action, while others have questioned the move or argued that the claims should be examined in court.For now, the dispute remains unresolved. Whether it leads to further legal proceedings may depend on what happens next, as both sides continue to address the controversy in public.
Article Summary: Kai Cenat’s legal team sent Reggie a cease-and-desist letter dated October 2, accusing him of making false and misleading statements online. The letter reportedly demands that Reggie stop repeating the disputed claims and remove social media content connected to them. Reggie has also released a YouTube music video for his track ‘Watch Me!’

Article Title: Protests sweep France, Spain as masked mobs loot shops, clash with cops; 1,100 held
Article Text:
In Barcelona, demonstrators taking part in a rally against the establishment set fire to street.

French riot police apprehend a protester amid clashes during demonstration organised by labour unions in Paris as part of nationwide protests called by the "Yellow Vests" movement.

A protester, wearing a gas mask and protective eyewear, drags a chair amidst tear gas, during a demonstration banned by local authorities and called by the "Yellow Vests" movement.

Tear gas and clashes in French cities

A protesters walks holding an umbrella next to a fire during an authorised demonstration organised by a labour union in Marseille.

Security tightened as unrest spreads

A vandalised store during a student's protest in Spain's Barcelona.

Anti-establishment demonstrations turned violent in France and Spain on Saturday, with protesters clashing with police, shops being looted and public property damaged.Authorities in Barcelona arrested 100 people after hooded demonstrators vandalised stores, while French police made nearly 1,000 arrests during protests over the cost of living and school funding.In Barcelona, demonstrators taking part in a rally against the establishment set fire to street furniture and looted shops around the central Plaza de Catalunya, an area popular with tourists and weekend shoppers.Catalonia's interior minister, Núria Parlon, said around a quarter of those arrested in Barcelona were minors. More than 30 fires were set and 14 shops were vandalised or looted, she added.The demonstrations were promoted on social media as a movement "against the system". Posts also used the slogan "Institut Indignats", a translation of "Lyceés Indignés", the name used by students who have protested in France in recent weeks. Both phrases refer to indignant or dissatisfied high school students.Videos shared online showed people trapped inside shops, including the department store El Corte Ingles, after shutters were lowered to prevent looting. Other footage showed hooded demonstrators dressed in black smashing shop windows and taking goods, sometimes encouraged by people watching online.Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni warned that acts of vandalism "will not go unpunished". He also said the guardians of minors involved could face legal consequences.In France, clashes broke out in Paris and several other cities as demonstrations against rising living costs and school funding drew hundreds of thousands of people. The protests, described by organisers as an “Acte II”, or second round, came a week after unrest involving widespread looting and damage to public buildings.The interior ministry estimated that 410,000 people took part nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris. The CGT union, which helped organise the demonstrations, put the national turnout at nearly 800,000 and the Paris crowd at 250,000. The ministry said turnout was lower than the 550,000 people it estimated had protested the previous weekend.The main Paris march began peacefully but descended into clashes near its endpoint in the east of the city. Masked protesters threw objects and fireworks at police, who responded with tear gas, sound grenades and water cannon. Officers used batons and charged at groups of demonstrators as the crowd dispersed.Police also used tear gas against protesters in Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had warned earlier in the day, “We will not tolerate any violence or any disturbance of public order.”Authorities deployed 70,000 security personnel across France to manage the demonstrations. The previous weekend's unrest had resulted in hundreds of shops being looted and 2,700 arrests.Also Read: France unrest: 70,000 police officers, weapons seized, nearly thousand protesters arrested - top developments The unrest in France appeared less violent as night fell, but clashes continued in several places. The demonstrations came six months before elections to choose a successor to President Emmanuel Macron, who is serving the final months of his term.Authorities restricted the main Paris march to the city's southeastern edge, away from the centre. Shops, including luxury boutiques, boarded up their windows and brought in extra security. The Louvre, Musée d'Orsay and Picasso Museum closed, while a scheduled football match between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais was postponed.In Barcelona, the scale of looting and damage prompted warnings from local authorities as footage of the unrest spread online. The protests in both countries reflected anger over different issues, with French demonstrators focusing on living costs and school funding, while the Barcelona rally was framed as a broader challenge to the establishment.
Article Summary: Around a quarter of those arrested in Barcelona were minors. More than 30 fires were set and 14 shops were vandalised or looted. Police used tear gas against protesters in Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.

Article Title: Watch: Iran mocks Trump on busy Tehran street, shows US president taking nap behind bars
Article Text:
A Trump impersonator rattles the bars of a mock jail cell and takes a nap inside a Tehran billboard targeting the US over a deadly strike on an Iranian wedding

A life-sized impersonator of US President Donald Trump has been put inside a jail-like cage mounted on a billboard in Tehran, where he can be seen rattling the bars and taking a nap in a staged display targeting Washington over a deadly strike on an Iranian wedding.The installation, placed above Tajrish Square, one of Tehran's busiest transport hubs, features an actor wearing a Trump mask and wig inside a mock prison cell equipped with a bed, toilet and sink. The performance has drawn crowds, with passersby stopping to film the spectacle.An electronic billboard behind the cage displays images related to a US strike that hit a wedding in the southern Iranian town of Kuhestak last month. The display also features crime-scene imagery, linking the attack to its message against the US president.The installation was unveiled on Tuesday by Tehran's Beautification Organization, which is affiliated with the city's municipality, according to Iranian state media. It appears to be part of a 15-day campaign highlighting the wedding strike.The display comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February.Also Read: 'Another little Epic Fury': Trump issues new warning; Iran says 'don't play with fire' Tehran has increasingly used public billboards to deliver political messages against Washington, including a previous display showing Trump lying in a graffiti-covered coffin.Iranian authorities and supporters have also circulated online memes and videos mocking Trump and his administration during the conflict.The wedding strike has become a focus of the latest campaign. US Central Command had said it was aware of Iranian reports about the incident and that American forces do not target civilians.
Article Summary: A life-sized impersonator of US President Donald Trump has been put inside a jail-like cage mounted on a billboard in Tehran. The performance has drawn crowds, with passersby stopping to film the spectacle. The display comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff firing: Turkish, desi pistols recovered in Surat, youth held in MP
Article Text:
Cops have arrested Pranjal Thakaran, a 22-year-old student, regarding the recent firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff

Turkish-made Zigana pistol used in past

‘MP youth was in contact with shooter who fired at Tiger’





MUMBAI: Cops investigating last Sunday's firing at actor Tiger Shroff arrested a 22-year-old student from Indore and recovered a Turkish-made Zigana pistol, a country-made firearm and 10 live cartridges from Surat. Pranjal Thakaran, who is pursuing engineering in Haryana's Sonipat, is the 11th suspect to be arrested in the case. He is suspected to be part of the support network and to have been in contact with a shooter, reports Mateen Hafeez.According to investigators, Thakaran's name surfaced during interrogation of the arrested accused and through technical evidence. A Mumbai police officer said his alleged links to the weapon supply chain were being examined.About the recovery of the weapons, sources said Mumbai police had taken the arrested shooters to Surat to find the spot where they had discarded the weapons. It took police around 8-10 hours to locate the firearms. The weapons and ammunition will be sent to the Kalina forensic science lab for ballistic analysis. Police sources say Lawrence Bishnoi gang has used the Zigana pistol in the past.The youth arrested from Indore, Pranjal Thakaran, was in contact with the person who allegedly carried out the firing at actor Tiger Shroff, preliminary questioning of the arrested suspects has indicated.However, investigators said his exact role in the conspiracy would be established only after further questioning.Thakaran, who is studying in Haryana, was arrested from a rehab centre in Indore. “Thakaran had arrived in Indore five days ago to meet his brother, who is undergoing treatment in the city,” said additional DCP Rajesh Dandotiya.The arrest followed inputs received by Mumbai Crime Branch about Thakaran’s presence in Indore. Dandotiya said Mumbai Crime Branch contacted its Indore counterparts on Thursday night, following which technical surveillance and other inputs helped trace his location. A joint team subsequently arrested him.Thakaran was produced before an Indore magistrate court, which granted him a three-day transit remand. He will be brought to Mumbai and produced before the Esplanade court for further remand proceedings.The arrest is part of a wider investigation into the Oct 18 firing outside a location in Juhu, where five to six rounds were fired at Shroff’s car. The actor escaped unhurt, while his driver and a vlogger sustained injuries. Investigators are probing the alleged conspiracy, the supply of weapons and the possible involvement of others in the attack.
Article Summary: Pranjal Thakaran, 22, is the 11th suspect to be arrested in the case. He is suspected to be part of the support network and to have been in contact with a shooter. Police recovered a Turkish-made Zigana pistol, a country-made firearm and 10 live cartridges from Surat.
